title: Founder of bankrupt Samson studio mulls how to use AI for his next attempt: 'Cutting corners in game development has a habit of coming back to bite you in the ass'
summary: Christopher Sundberg said the goal for his next studio is to make "a game we can afford to finish without needing every sales forecast to come true."
body: Christofer Sundberg, the founder of Samson developer Liquid Swords, has confirmed the studio's closure, saying that while the console version of the game enjoyed "much greater success" than the PC release, it "wasn't enough to get the company across the finish line." Reports over the weekend revealed that Liquid Swords had gone bankrupt just six months after the PC release of Samson, which was followed by a console launch in September. "It's been a hell of a ride and a lot of fun, even when the circumstances gave us very little to laugh about," Sundberg wrote. "Building a studio, creating Samson and releasing it on PC and consoles took an enormous amount of work from people who cared deeply about what we were making. "The console versions met with much greater success than the PC release. We got them out, but that success wasn't enough to get the company across the finish line. Market conditions and some bad business decisions brought us here, and I own my part in that. I can look honestly at what went wrong and still be proud of what we built." Samson wasn't especially well received when it debuted on PCs, and while post-launch updates have tightened it up, it still holds a very …

title: I have neither the budget nor the inclination for a crystal encrusted RTX 5090, but Galax is releasing one anyway
summary: These stones ain't no friends of mine.
body: Nvidia's RTX 5090 GPU has become particularly elusive lately. In light of swirling rumours, Nvidia promises the 5090 isn't dead but constrained supply and runaway pricing has made it a tough card to track down. So, amidst all of this, what does Palit-owned hardware manufacturer Galax do? Tease a gem-studded edition of the RTX 5090. The GeForce RTX 5090 Hall of Fame Edition was technically already teased back during Computex, though folks thought this showfloor piece was alluding to a whole new GPU generation at the time . Now, we know this special edition is actually current gen and will feature a GPU shroud encrusted with Swarovski crystals (via Techpowerup ). No price has yet been announced ahead of this exceptionally extra card's slated October 22 release date. With how much a standard RTX 5090 costs, odds are that those planning to scoop this shiny GPU will need very deep pockets indeed. For context, we've stopped including the RTX 5090 in the graphics card price watch , as our Dave notes the card is 'unavailable' from many reputable retailers. title: Microsoft won't like this open source project to get Game Pass working on SteamOS and Linux, but I think it's pretty neat
summary: If it doesn't exist, build it yourself.
body: It wasn't long ago that Linux gaming was considered fairly niche—but given that Windows 11 is unpopular with many, it seems that not a day goes by without something regarding the switch to Linux hitting my newsfeed. Not to mention the continuing updates to Valve's Arch-based SteamOS. Now my attention has been drawn to the Xodus Nexus , an experimental open-source project that aims to allow Linux and SteamOS users to access PC Game Pass. This includes the ability to browse, install, and launch games via a very familiar interface, complete with cloud save support. That's for supported games only, of course, but the GitHub page has a big long list of them. From Gears of War: E-Day , to Minecraft for Windows, to Halo: Campaign Evolved , there sure are some big hitters that are already supported by the open-source platform. The readme describes the project as "An Xbox-inspired launcher built on Xodus , using our patched Nexus backend and Nexus runtime. Browse the store, install games you own or can access through a subscription, and play with one shared runtime." The whole system seems to be in an experimental test phase at the moment, and the controller navigation looks to be a work i…

title: Amnesia: The Dark Descent's co-founder explained the 'the dynamic of Steam' to Red Barrels after Outlast's sales slowed down
summary: "Basically, your sales curve becomes like a roller coaster."
body: Three of the most influential games from my childhood were Pokémon HeartGold, Amnesia: The Dark Descent , and Outlast . Knowing this, you could probably piece together the kind of person I have become—let's just say it explains a lot. So it brought a smile to my face when I learned that without one of these influential games, I wouldn't have had the other—no, Pokémon HeartGold has nothing to do with anything—it's actually Amnesia which helped bring Outlast to the world. Red Barrels, the Outlast devs, already discussed how difficult it was to pitch Outlast to publishers in an interview with GameSpot . But they also mentioned how Amnesia: The Dark Descent was something of a lodestar for the team. (Image credit: Red Barrels) Not only did the success of Amnesia reassure Red Barrels that there was in fact a market for the kind of game they were trying to make, but the fact that no one else had really tried to ride its coattails meant there was a space left wide open for them. Some of the Red Barrels devs even sat in on a conference talk where Frictional Games co-founder Thomas Grip revealed that Amnesia: The Dark Descent sold an impressive 400,000 copies in its first year. title: Moonlighter studio won't host a public playtest of its next game due to rampant AI-led cloning: 'We know we're not the only developers feeling this way'
summary: ReVamp will get a limited Discord playtest.
body: The studio behind the Moonlighter series has announced it will no longer host a public playtest for its forthcoming roguelike due to fears it will be "reverse-engineered, cloned and published". The move comes as a surge in rapidly vibe coded clones floods Steam, Roblox and mobile app stores in the aftermath of Claude Opus 5.5. "With launch still months away, sharing a build with tens of thousands of players feels like too big a risk," Digital Sun Games' marketing manager Israel Mallén told PC Gamer. The game under discussion is ReVamp , a "tower defensevania" roguelike due for release in March 2027. "We know we're not the only developers feeling this way, and the more this is talked about, the more likely platforms are to step in." In its public announcement Digital Sun Games was fairly blunt. "We've been concerned by recent news of games being reverse-engineered, cloned and published before the original is even out. With launch still months away, a large public build of ReVamp felt like too big a risk." Last week the studio behind Drunken Goddess Reflux canceled plans to roll out a public demo for Steam Next Fest due to similar fears. "We're concerned the demo's content could be …

title: Xbox biz guy deletes his X account less than 24 hours after saying game devs who don't embrace AI 'should not be in the business of being a business'
summary: Business strategy manager Brandon Stirrup said he was "happy to take the hit" for his stance on AI, then left social media.
body: Xbox senior business strategy manager Brandon Stirrup is tired of pussyfooting around about AI: In a thread on X his week, he said that he wants the world to know that Xbox uses it, that he thinks everyone should be using it, and that he believes so strongly in the cause that he's willing to "take the hit" for saying so. He has since deleted his X account. A source at Xbox tells PC Gamer that Stirrup opted to deactivate the account because of the volume of replies he was receiving. Stirrup kicked off his thread on October 18 with a simple message saying he'd "vibe coded a bad but improvable game" over two days, although he only "actively" worked on it for about three hours. "I’m telling you I tried it and it’s true…anyone can build a game." After saying that developers and studios who aren't incorporating AI into their strategies are "planning for a fake future," Stirrup went all in. "Look if I'm fired tomorrow it will be because I told you the truth that nobody wants you to know. You can make a game with a simple prompt and yes you can make custom, tailored games. Everything you want in a game is right there for the taking, for better or worse," he wrote. "I'm happy to take the h…

summary: Own up, which one of you was it?
body: Good news: I know of the existence of two entire pallets worth of RTX 5090 graphics cards—a rare thing in this day and age, as stock appears to have dwindled to virtually zero . Bad news, they've 'gone missing' from a Brazilian airport. Brazilian electronics distributor Oderço has published an Instagram post drawing attention to the missing Zotac GPUs, which supposedly arrived at Guarulhos International Airport in São Paulo, but then promptly vanished. "In our more than 38-year history, we have never encountered a situation like this—and we will not remain silent," says CEO Oderço Matos (via Tom's Hardware , machine translation). "Two pallets of Zotac RTX 5090 graphics cards have gone missing at Guarulhos International Airport. The merchandise is worth approximately R$2.5 million (at cost), and to date, we have received no answers." "We are seeking clarification and want to understand what happened," Matos continues. "How can a shipment of such value disappear from within an international airport without any explanation being provided to us?" body: Play This Right Now Welcome to Play This Right Now, the site version of our weekly newsletter in which we celebrate a new game, update, or DLC that we think is well worth checking out. It's utter chaos. We fight further and further into the ship, unlocking platforms, defeating waves of enemies and giant turrets which pop out of the deck to gun down unsuspecting looters. But I think we're done. Time is running short and we've once again stalled at this stage of the puzzle. title: Clive Barker says he's 'genuinely astonished' by Hellraiser: Revival: 'I'm proud as f**k at the end result'
summary: "I think what was achieved in the game is a wake-up call".
body: Hellraiser: Revival's commitment to being both gnarly and horny has already been thoroughly documented, with PC Gamer's Wes Fenlon describing it as " nasty nasty" in his preview . This uncompromising attitude to both gore and kink went down well with fans, but it has also been celebrated by Hellraiser's creator, Clive Barker. In an interview with horror site Dread Central (via FRVR ), Barker admitted that he had concerns about the project going into it, but was thoroughly impressed by the final product. "I'm proud as f**k at the end result," he said. "I was fearful at one point that the game would be overly censored, but I'm genuinely astonished by how far they've been able to push it." Barker, who worked closely with developer Saber Interactive to shape Revival's world and to advise on the game's story, reckons that Saber Interactive's work on the game is a prime example of how to approach adapting a license. "I think what was achieved in the game is a wake-up call to anyone who's been involved in the making of a franchise like Hellraiser," the author and director explained. Barker reclaimed the American franchise rights to Hellraiser several years ago, and Hellraiser: Revival is…

title: Liquid Swords, developer of open-city crime sim Samson, has gone bankrupt following staff claims that they haven't been paid in two months
summary: The administrator is currently seeking a buyer for the studio and its assets.
body: Liquid Swords, the developer behind Samson , has gone bankrupt just six months after its run-based open-city crime sim was released. As reported by Breakit (via Rock, Paper, Shotgun ), a bankruptcy order was issued against the Swedish developer on October 12. According to Breakit, Liquid Swords' staff—around 30 employees—have gone unpaid for at least two months, and it was those employees who petitioned to have the company declared bankrupt. Liquid Swords was founded in 2020 by Christofer Sundberg, who previously co-founded Just Cause developer Avalanche Studios and co-directed that series' first game. Samson was Liquid Swords' debut title, an open city-crime sim with a distinctive run-based structure, where you play a getaway driver attempting to pay back an enormous mob debt by any means necessary. Samson was a difficult project for Sundberg and Liquid Swords. The studio initially intended for it to be a much larger action RPG. But the studio struggled to find a publisher for Samson, with one publisher rejecting Liquid Swords on five occasions. Last year, Liquid Swords ran into funding trouble, laying off half its team as a result. It also radically adjusted how Samson plays—whi…

title: Metal band Genitorturers claims a Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remake is coming, getting a dozen crusty nerds way too worked up
summary: I'm one of a dozen crusty nerds.
body: Original Story: This one is thin , man, but it has to do with one of my favorite games of all time , while the circumstances of the rumor are just kind of neat and weird, even if it turns out to be nothing. User Few_Interview8222 on the Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines subreddit reported back from a Genitorturers show in Brooklyn, New York. Partway through the set, the band supposedly told the crowd that a VtMB remake is happening. Genitorturers played at Brooklyn's The Meadows as part of their "Live + Lewd Tour" on October 15. We've reached out to both rights-holder Activision (one of several, it's complicated) and Genitorturers' representation, and will update this story if we hear back. Why would an industrial metal band started in Orlando in 1986 have this information? In addition to a killer score by Rik Schaffer , Bloodlines featured wonderfully era-appropriate licensed tracks from metal bands⁠—they were mostly used as diegetic music in the nightclubs and bars of Los Angeles. title: Qualcomm wins $2 legal decision against fellow tech giant Arm, and that's not a typo
summary: It's not just the principle of the thing: There could be more money up for grabs.
body: At a glance: Qualcomm gets $2 from Arm in the Delaware jury's decision, part of a yearslong licensing dispute between the two. Yahoo Finance puts their market caps at $210 billion and $243 billion respectively. Qualcomm alleges bad faith action by Arm over tech licensed by the former company from the latter. Qualcomm won $1 on its allegations of Arm withholding contractually obligated support on the licensed tech, and $1 on allegations Arm interfered with a deal between Qualcomm and Meta. Still undecided: Does Qualcomm get a 5-year pause on licensing payments to Arm, which could total in the billions of dollars? Reuters reported on the mystifying reward, which makes much more sense in the context of a broader legal battle between Qualcomm and Arm. The two companies are each behind some of the most widely-used processors in the world: Qualcomm's Snapdragon CPUs can be found in most non-Apple smartphones. Arm's titular architecture, meanwhile, is the basis of the Snapdragon CPU, and there are rumblings the future of desktop computing belongs to Arm and not the x86 architecture we've defaulted to for so long. The Delaware jury found that Arm breached a licensing agreement with Qualco…
